summary:
No region-specific legal divergence is identified in the source material for the Comunidad Foral de Navarra. The region is recorded as standing under Spain's national framework for gender recognition and LGBTI rights, and no Navarran statute, court ruling or administrative practice departing from it appears in the inventory. Visitor-facing practice in Navarra is therefore the practice applied across Spain, and nothing in the material changes the national assessment of risk or access.

Diario de Navarra reported on 12 May 2026 that Navarra planned to create an observatory against LGBTI-phobia, a measure that remained at the planning stage at that date. No regional equality body of this kind is recorded as operating in Navarra at that point.
tangentialFactors: Navarra holds the earliest documented prosecutions for same-sex acts in the Iberian peninsula. In 1290 a Muslim man was burned at Arguedas for 'yacer con otros'; in 1345 Juce Abolfaça and Simuel Nahamán, two Jews of Olite, were tortured into confessions and burned before a cortege of twenty for the crime of sodomy. Both episodes belong to the pre-modern criminal order and are the earliest legal record on the subject in the region; they form no part of the framework applied in Navarra now.
localsOnly: Navarra has its own regional LGBTI equality legislation, Ley Foral 8/2017. The inventory does not set out its provisions, so the obligations it places on regional services and the entitlements it gives residents of Navarra cannot be stated here. Residents otherwise stand under the same national framework that applies across Spain.
outOfScopeNotes:
The content of Navarra's own Ley Foral 8/2017 is not substantively covered in the material; its provisions and the regional obligations it creates are unresolved.

A 2025 observatory report is referenced alongside the announced regional observatory, and the inventory records that the two sit in tension. The material does not establish the report's findings or how the two relate, so that point is unresolved.

No Navarran court ruling, regional enforcement action or trans-specific incident appears in the material; region-level enforcement of the national hate-crime provisions cannot be assessed from this inventory.
